sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed: monoclonal antibodies raised against the FLAG-tagged construct recognise native ART4 on the surface of living cells, indicating correct folding and trafficking. ADP-ribosyltransferase enzymatic activity was NOT MEASURED in this clip.
sites.rationale: ART4 is GPI-anchored; the signal peptide (residues 1–46) is cleaved at the N-terminus and the GPI anchor signal at the C-terminus is also cleaved, leaving no free C-terminal surface handle. The only extracellular terminus available for a surface tag is immediately after the SP cleavage site. Python confirmed residue 46 = G (last SP residue) and residue 47 = S (first mature residue); insert_after_residue = 46 places the tag at the mature N-terminus, consistent with standard GPI-protein tagging practice. The paper's confirmation that mAbs against the FLAG-tagged construct recognise native ART4 on living cells validates surface display and correct folding of the tagged protein. Stable transfectants of full-length human ART4 (CD297) carrying a FLAG tag were generated; the tagged construct is membrane-anchored and surface-displayed, confirmed by monoclonal antibodies that recognise native ART4 on living cells. No residue number is stated in the clip. ART4 is GPI-anchored: the C-terminus carries the GPI anchor signal (cleaved and replaced by GPI lipid), so a C-terminal tag would be removed. The sole viable extracellular terminus for a surface-displayed tag is after the signal peptide cleavage site (after residue 46, the last SP residue G, before residue 47, the mature N-terminus S).

sources.claim: ART2-which has sparked interest because of its ability to activate the cytolytic P2X7 purinergic receptor by ADP-ribosylation-is encoded by two functional gene copies in the mouse genome while the human genome carries two inactivated ART2 pseudogenes. We generated stable transfectants for FLAG-tagged versions of each of the functional human and mouse ARTs. Using genetic immunization we raised monoclonal antibodies that recognize the native human ARTs on the surface of living cells.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is provided. It reports FLAG-tagged full-length human ART4 with confirmed surface display but names no insertion residue. Because ART4 is GPI-anchored, the C-terminus is occupied by the GPI anchor signal (cleaved in the ER and replaced by the GPI lipid moiety); any C-terminal tag would be removed co-translationally and could not appear on the cell surface. The N-terminal position after signal peptide cleavage (after residue 46) is therefore the only topology-consistent location for the observed surface-displayed FLAG tag, making this a topology_derived rather than validated site. No internal loop insertions are supported by the ledger.
